summary: US-CH1: Channel registry — a channel becomes a defined thing in catalog
description:
Today `channel_code` is an exact opaque string duplicated across four tables in three services (`claims`, `channel_allocations`, `fee_rules`, `split_schedules`), each with a comment saying the bounds must agree, and nothing defines what a channel *is*. This story creates the registry: an organizer-scoped catalog table of channels with a code, a display name, a kind, and an enabled flag, plus the reads that let the rest of the platform resolve a code to a definition.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A `channels` table in catalog, organizer-scoped, with `code` (the same 1..100 exact opaque string bound the four existing tables use), `display_name`, `kind` (`web` | `pos` | `presale` | `reseller`), `enabled`, and standard timestamps. Unique on (organizer_id, code).
- Catalog exposes CRUD over the registry: create, list, get, update. Codes are immutable after creation (a rename is a new channel) — attempting to change one is refused.
- A public read returns only enabled channels and their display names, in ADR-004's tier with an explicit `Cache-Control`; the operator read (internal) returns everything including disabled.
- **No FK from `claims`, `channel_allocations`, `fee_rules` or `split_schedules` to the registry.** ADR-024 forbids it for `claims` (historical attribution must survive a channel being deleted); the same argument extends to the rest. The registry is a lookup, not a constraint — an unregistered code keeps working exactly as it does today.
- A migration backfills nothing and changes no existing table.
- Tests: the code-immutability refusal, the enabled/disabled split between the two reads, the uniqueness constraint per organizer, and a test asserting an unregistered channel code still sells (the no-FK guarantee).

Quality gates: `make check` green; contract tests for the touched catalog boundary; OpenAPI regenerated and committed before the gate; new public read declares its ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale.

Parent: TKT-17. Non-goals: per-channel pricing (US-CH3), windows (US-CH4), presale codes (US-CH5), reseller API (US-CH6), any back-office UI (US-CH2).

objective.note: Four tables carry an opaque channel_code and nothing defines a channel. Every later story in this epic needs a definition to hang behavior off. This is the prefactor slice.

scope.note: IN: channels table (organizer-scoped), catalog CRUD, public enabled-only read + internal full read, ADR-004 tier, migration. OUT: pricing axis, windows, presale codes, reseller API, UI, any FK or enforcement against existing channel_code columns.

uncertainties.note: Resolved by reading: the 1..100 bound is set in services/inventory/.../0004_channel_allocations.sql, catalog 0016_fee_rules.sql:57 and 0017_payees_and_split_schedules.sql:60 — the registry mirrors it rather than inventing one. `kind` is a closed enum here; extending it later is additive.

dependencies.note: None open. Builds on shipped TKT-78/TKT-214/TKT-216 substrate; blocks every other child of TKT-17.

approach.note: New catalog migration + store + API, mirroring the shape of 0016_fee_rules.sql and its store/api pair. Deliberately additive: no existing table is altered, so no existing sale path changes behavior. Verified against the code — the four channel_code columns are independent and uncoerced today, so a lookup-only registry is genuinely non-breaking.

first_slice.note: This IS the first slice — table + CRUD + reads, demoable by creating a channel and listing it.

success.note: COS above; the load-bearing one is the no-FK test proving an unregistered code still sells.

binding.rule: Money is represented as integer minor units + ISO currency code everywhere; floats are banned on money paths.

governingAdrs.why: Catalog owns rule and entity definitions; commerce owns pricing/fee/promo evaluation. A channel registry is a definition and belongs in catalog.

Channel codes are exact opaque strings — no normalization, no case folding; a registry must not introduce an FK from claims (historical attribution) nor a counter; release stays a clock_timestamp() predicate under the pool FOR UPDATE.
OpenAPI is the source of truth; generated code must be committed before the gate or check-generate reads the regen as drift.
Every public read endpoint declares a volatility-tiered TTL with explicit Cache-Control.
Catalog's public read cache machinery — a new public catalog read joins its tier discipline.
Inventory availability cache is channel-keyed with a 128-entry per-slot bound; a registry must not let arbitrary channel strings cache-through.

reference.summary: PRD v1 — TKT-17 capability row + US-015 non-goals (registry/pricing/windows stay in TKT-17)

### ✅ Implementation readiness — PASS

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | ✅ | Registry is the prefactor every other child needs |
| Scope | ✅ | Additive only — no existing table altered |
| Uncertainties | ✅ | Length bound and enum resolved by reading the three existing migrations |
| Dependencies | ✅ | No open blockers; blocks US-CH2..CH6 |
| Approach | ✅ | Verified: the four channel_code columns are independent today, so a lookup-only registry is non-breaking |
| First slice | ✅ | Table + CRUD + reads, demoable standalone |
| Success | ✅ | COS verifiable; no-FK test is the load-bearing one |
| Context-mémo | ✅ | Baked, 6 governing ADRs each resolving to a real file at HEAD |

**Concerns:** none.
**Verdict:** PASS — smallest safe slice of TKT-17 and the prefactor for the rest.
